reviews.text: After taking our pug to two different emergency animal clinics to treat his bladder stones, we almost gave up on getting our boy the treatment he needed.  We called VEG and they connected us straight to the surgeon and we had him there in less than 30 mins.  He was taken back immediately and they started to work on our boy.  I’m so grateful for the courteous staff and amazing doctor who did his surgery.  We were charged 2k by one clinic and 8k by another and neither had a surgeon on staff as they said they did.  We are so lucky to have found VEG, would highly recommend.  Their prices are super affordable and their staff is incredible !

My cat was in respiratory distress and the VEG team saw her right away and gave her a thorough evaluation and testing while trying to make a very stressed kitty who hates the vet feel as comfortable as possible. I really appreciate how everyone in the team stepped in through the process to help and give Pancake what she needed!

Unfortunately our dog developed pneumonia 3 days before our wedding. The staff was so unbelievably helpful and even set us up in a little honeymoon suite with a pullout bed so we could stay as she was getting treatment. We were discharged this morning and they even went and got us cakes and some potted succulents as a wedding gift. I am blown away at how kind and thoughtful they were and the gestures at the end were so immensely appreciated.  Our dog is doing worlds better and they truly were the cornerstone of turning this rough situation into a special moment. Thank you so much

Decent enough vet but be prepared for them to blatantly ignore you while you sit there for hours on end. Make sure you are okay with being forgotten about in the exam room for two hours while the nurses lie to you about “being right back”

Truly one of the Best.
I've never felt more at ease and comfortable with people whom had the care of my pet.
Confidence & Trust was easily given.
These people care as if it was their pet on the table.
If for some unfortunate reason an E.R. vet is needed I would strongly suggest VEG animal hospital. I'm very grateful that they are here.
Right from the start I told them my financial concerns, considering what I might be facing, they made me comfortable about it, and all worked out well.
Very compassionate people. A blessing.
I couldn't speak higher of them.

Sure enough, when Chiika got home, she started having her breathng difficulty symptom again, But I could rest assured knowing I had the support I needed—unlike other vets in the past who wouldn't give me any information or guidance for home, making those visits feel pointless and costly.
​This team left me completely confident that she is going to be okay. Now I just need our apartment management to do their part, as we just moved in. I'm praying they are as kindhearted as this vet and vet nurse were in putting her well-being above everything else.
​Thank you so much to Dr. Logan and her nurse—you guys are forever appreciated! If you ever need to bring your pet in for an emergency visit, or if you want a team that truly cares about your furry baby as much as you do, this is absolutely where you need to go.

​★★★★★ Exceptional, compassionate care when I needed it most
​If you need an emergency or urgent vet team you can truly trust, look no further than VEG ER for Pets on Camelback Rd. Moving into a new apartment with a tight budget and facing a scary health issue with my cat was overwhelming, especially after negative experiences elsewhere where clinics just took fees without providing real answers.
​From the start, this team was incredibly understanding of my situation. I explained my financial situation and tried to find a vet that would see her with a free first exam, and they were so kind to quickly put me through to the doctor. Instead of brushing me off, they connected me directly with Dr. Logan. Over the phone, Dr. Logan truly listened to my concerns and walked through clear, reassuring steps to evaluate if my cat needed to be seen immediately. I have never experienced a vet taking the time to do that before.
​I quickly brought her in to rule out abdominal bleeding, and Dr. Logan did a full exam from the inside out on my furry baby. Thankfully, it was all good news—it turns out it was environmental issues from our recent move into the new apartment! Other vets would have left me struggling in financial hardship just to get a diagnosis—which I barely even got—making it impossible to afford treatment afterward. In the past, other doctors didn't give me any remedies or advice on what I could get for her—like when she had an arm injury, they wouldn't even give me pain advice or bandage her, only pushing for $1,500 X-rays I couldn't afford. But not Dr. Logan. She didn't just look at the immediate moment; she addressed what was happening at home and gave me clear directions on how to keep her safe and what I could and could not give her.
​Dr. Logan is hands-down one of the most genuine, caring veterinarians in the business. It is obvious she genuinely cares about animals and understands how much our pets mean to us as family. If you want someone to care about your pet as much as you do, this is where to take them. I highly, highly recommend them because my pet is my everything. Thank you so much, Dr. Logan and the team at VEG ER for Pets, for giving me peace of mind and being there for us

I arrived with my pet after he was bit by another dog and was seen immediately. There is a  glass room before entering the waiting room which gave my dog a chance to be visually assessed. He was weighed, sedated and received 3 stitches. The doctor removed skin before stitching to minimize infection.  We completed the treatment within 3 hours. The room was clean and the emergency room staff was helpful.

I wanted to share my experience here, as I have visited this hospital twice within a 72-hour period.

I initially brought my 10-month-old kitten to the ER around 9 p.m. on Thursday due to a distended abdomen. Over the course of the evening, I interacted with both a nurse and a doctor regarding his care. I won’t lie; we were there for over four hours. However, it was very apparent that the staff was spread thin, and the hospital was busy. They performed bloodwork and other evaluations, and the nurse who cared for him was particularly attentive throughout the visit.

Fast forward approximately 48 hours. After a full day of work and being out for a birthday celebration, I came home to find that the paw used for his blood draw was nearly three times the size of his other paws. The bandage from his blood draw had been left on, and because he is long-haired, I hadn’t noticed it. Naturally, I panicked. This is my baby, and seeing his paw in that condition was incredibly upsetting.

I immediately called the hospital to explain what had happened. I’ll admit that I was upset, and understandably so. My initial conversation was with a different doctor, who I found to be incredibly dismissive. I don’t know her name, or I would gladly include it here. I eventually requested to speak with whoever was the highest-ranking person on the floor. I was then connected with Serena, the original nurse who had cared for him. She openly acknowledged that she had forgotten to remove the bandage.

We brought him back to the hospital immediately for an evaluation. Serena greeted us at the door and made sure we were taken care of as soon as we arrived.

Ultimately, I wanted to write this review because of Serena. She owned up to her mistake, was genuinely apologetic, and continued to show care and concern for my kitten throughout the entire process. I think she is an exceptional nurse. She could have avoided facing me after what happened, but she didn’t. She took accountability, treated us with kindness, and made sure my baby was cared for. I have an enormous amount of respect for that.

I also hope this incident serves as a reminder that veterinary professionals, particularly technicians and nurses, work long, demanding hours, often in the middle of the night, and are frequently overworked and underpaid. They are human, and mistakes happen. Accountability and compassion matter, and Serena demonstrated both. I only wish the doctor I initially spoke with had shown even a fraction of the understanding and professionalism that Serena did. I hope she can learn something from her.

I will likely not return to this hospital, but if I ever do, I will absolutely be asking for Serena. If you have the opportunity to have her care for your pet, I would recommend her without hesitation.

I had such a positive experience with VEG during what was an incredibly scary time for us. Remy was triaged immediately when we arrived, and it wasn’t long before a veterinarian came over to speak with me and explain what was going on.

Remy ended up being admitted and spent four nights in the hospital, so we interacted with many different vets and vet techs during our stay. Every single person we encountered was amazing. Everyone was compassionate, attentive, communicative, and genuinely seemed to care about Remy.

I especially appreciated being able to stay close to him throughout his hospitalization. I spent the last 32 hours there with him in one of the rooms, with Remy by my side, until he was finally doing well enough to be discharged. Being able to be there with him meant so much to me.

The entire team made an extremely stressful situation easier, and I felt confident that Remy was receiving excellent care. They even rolled out the red carpet for him when he was discharged, which was such a sweet way to end four very difficult days.

I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who helped care for Remy. Thank you for taking such good care of him and for being so kind to both of us.

This is an amazing veterinary emergency practice.  I had the pleasure of observing them at work while I awaited bloodwork results for the foster furbaby I had brought in.  Their professionalism, compassion, competence and attentiveness to each pet and pet parent went far beyond the call of duty. They provided excellent care for my kitty and for all the patients I observed while I was there.

They will rip you off because they know you have no other choice to save your pet. My vet when open charges under $1000 for a procedure. Same procedure here is at least $7,000. I can understand extra cost for an emergency, but this is bilking people one what could be one of the worst days of their lives if you don't pay up.

HORRIBLE ETHICS. This is what we get when corporate interests take over pet care.

DO NOT RECOMMEND.

We had an unexpected emergency with our 15-year-old girl and had to bring her in well past midnight, staying until almost 3 a.m. From the moment we arrived, we were met immediately by the triage team, who checked her vitals and did their due diligence to make sure our baby girl got the care and attention she needed. Everyone was incredibly kind, thorough, and reassuring during a very stressful night. The whole team was great, and we’re so grateful they were there when we needed them!

Really a Compassionate, Competent and efficient experience during a very stressful time.  Highly recommended and so happy they are available in emergencies.

Thank you to all that helped us today!!

My dog had to be put down this weekend early in the morning around 4:30am. The doctor gave me all the options and the entire staff was absolutely amazing. There was a younger kid that helped us into the private room where you can be with you pet for their last moments and he was a very compassionate and helpful and he really helped me through it. I have brought Rosie here a few times and every time was a great experience. Thank you for being so kind and caring to my girl in her last moments.

The 2 stars are for why though the service was good, I wouldn’t go back there. I took my dog lucky about a month ago for seizures, and it was his first time he had two seizures in 24 hours and he was not on medication, the way they explained it was it’s an emergency and he needs to be hospitalized right away, and I never had any experience dealing with it so I joined and him and the bill they gave was around $3300 if he was hospitalized for 24 hours and said he could return in 12 hours if he  doesn’t have another seizure and that it would cost $2200. They wouldn’t start treatment until I paid $3300 and then next day I got the $1000 refund, all they did was give him kappera and some anxiety medicine. I think that’s rip off, they didn’t even have a payment plan. Now that I have learnt more about seizures and lucky clustered again multiple times and was hospitalized at Thrive, I know it was a rip off. Overnight stay at thrive costed half of VEG price - I literally paid less than $1000 for recent seizures clustering with neurologist checking on lucky. So as much as they are good, the fact that they are insanely expensive and do not really educate you on the problem, choices you have and kinda make it sound like admitting is the only option is highly unethical. Second time I took lucky to thrive, the doctor was honest about his condition and said just add this medication and he’ll be fine. And he was , following that weeks later he needed to be admitted and they were honest about it too. Folks at VEG are not , as kind as they sound and good at what they do. I was disappointed afterwards.

Our dog was bit by coyotes early in the morning. The staff immediately saw us, we were able to stay with Zuko to comfort him as he does get a little anxious in new spaces, and the care he received was amazing. The facility was clean, the staff was efficient in providing the exact care he needed and they even allowed my son (when appropriate) to participate (like listening to heart beat, holding the blood pressure cuff, etc), which really helped calm his fears as well. For such a scary situation we felt so cared for. Could not recommend this facility more!

My sweet, 11.5 year old golden, Charlie had to cross the rainbow bridge this morning. Our regular veterinarian is out with an emergency so his office directed us to VEG. I have never been there before so I was nervous about it. They were incredible. Kind, compassionate and understanding. Obviously, I hope we never need an emergency room again but if we do, we know where to go. Thank you to the staff at VEG. The Serna family is very appreciative of the gentle care you gave our boy.

My sweet boy Major recently passed away from parvo. We brought him to this hospital desperately hoping they would be able to save his life. Although we had no money upfront, we managed to secure credit to help cover his expenses. You should have seen the front desk lady's face—how it completely lit up the second we told her we had been approved for credit to pay them. They charged us $4,600 for just 24 hours of care.
After those 24 hours passed, they cornered us with cruel options: somehow come up with more money to keep him there, or put him down.
Major suffered immensely because of their incompetence. The staff forcefully tried putting a feeding tube through his nose, and he bled for a good while. They didn't even know what they were doing—it took three different people to try and put it in, and all they did was hurt him. Especially the morning doctor, who added to our distress. They kept telling us they tried feeding him but that he would throw it up, which was a complete lie. The entire time we were there, he never once threw up. They were only keeping him hydrated and failed to give him proper, active treatment for parvo.
All they care about is your money. If you don’t have it, they do not care. They do not care about your pets unless you have deep pockets. Please think twice before bringing your beloved animal here.

Took my 17 y/o cat there one morning after coming home and finding her with an avulsion injury to her foot. When we got there we were met at the door and triaged immediately. Everyone we saw from the front desk staff to the nurses to the doctor were amazing. I have to give to shout-out to Dr. Megan Helgerson; she stitched my cat's foot (those stitches were clean af too, I was very impressed) and her bedside manner was great - very knowledgeable, explained everything, and responsive to questions., We had to make multiple trips back and she tracked our baby's progress the whole way. We also saw another doctor in between visits, I can't remember her name, but she was great also; Dr. Helgerson gave her report so she would know what to expect and I really appreciated that. I would and have 100% recommended this vet ER to everyone I know, great experience from start to finish. It's one of those things you hope you'll never need but when you do, it's great knowing these guys are there.

Taking your furbaby in for any suspected emergency is never an easy thing to do, especially financially. I had a previous bad experience with another establishment and would prefer avoiding an emergency visit at all costs but the wellbeing of my pet is more important. Luna had suddenly swelled up in the face to where her eyes were barely visible and knew she needed to be seen asap. I had seen VEG a time or two while in the area and thought I'd give them a try. Best decision ever. From the moment I walked in, the health of my pet was their #1 priority. Being able to stay with her every step of the way and seeing the interaction between the other families  made it very comforting. It's good to know there are still people who genuinely love their jobs and the animals they treat.
Excellent emergency vet service. Compassionate employees!

Hi Xalen,

Thank you for your fantastic 5-star rating! 

 Nichole Collen, Hospital Manager
1st time patient and I was blown away by the facility and how everyone approached me and Phoenyx with care. The whole night staff was kind.
Highly recommend.  They have treated and saved my dog multiple times with his disease.  Many thanks. Best ever

Haven't physically been here.

Called with a general question about Arizona vs Texas scorpions. The receptionist was not able to answer my question, but I was quickly transferred to a technician. I felt a lot better after our chat. I appreciate the time she took to talk to me. I would be willing to bring my pet here if the need arose.

- Former Vet Tech of 8+ years

In our worst moment sitting with our sick puppy all the employees were kind and understanding. The vet was very knowledgeable and gave us multiple options that suited us. Would highly recommend bringing your pet here if you have an emergency!

The whole staff and team at VEG were extremely helpful, friendly, and overall amazing. Everyone there, all of the doctors, nurses, and techs went above and beyond to care for my dog and make sure he was going to be ok. You truly saved his life and I’m beyond grateful. I cannot express my gratitude enough. I already have been telling everyone about the amazing service I received, and I cannot recommend you guys enough. Thank you!

I just got home after a very quick visit. My new kitten had a low appetite, thew up.  I panicked and brought her to the vet right away. I think she just needed time to adapt to the new im environment.  The nurse took vitals and examined her and said she was normal and gave me samples of different kitten foods for her to try. They let me keep a little towel since she was shivering. Then they no-charged the visit since I didn’t see a vet. It was so busy and I am very grateful for a kind vet nurse, my only regret is I didn’t give her a hug!

I will now monitor the kitten and will definitely be returning back to this emergency vet if needed.

Hi James,

Thank you for your 5 star review!

Nichole Collen, Hospital Manager

I have taken all my pets at some point to these folks who are absolutely fantastic. Very caring, welcoming, and you don't feel trapped in a closed room. I completely trust them with my pets emergencies.

My dog was bitten by a pitbull on our walk. It was a traumatic experience and we were met at VEG with such service and compassion. Every single staff we came in contact with was incredibly kind, genuine and knowledgeable. To say they went above and beyond would be an understatement. I just wanted to say thank you from the bottom of my heart for treating Oreo and I with so much respect and compassion!
Incredible staff. Extremely kind and polite. Handled my little guy with extreme care.

VEG has helped my cat twice over the years and we would absolutely recommend them for emergency care. The open layout style can be unexpected but it allowed me to stay with my cat throughout treatment and helped me understand what was happening. It was a gift.

Blown away by the service at this emergency vet. I have a very— vet— reactive pitbull mix and the staff was wonderful and accommodating. The doctor was knowledgeable and explained everything thoroughly. I got to stay with my dog even while she was heavily sedated and they were placing stitches. I will recommend this place to all of my family and friends needing emergency vet care.

All the staff were truly wonderful. I am so grateful to the tech (?, not sure that is her title, but had a long blonde braid.) She worked with me after Bella’s treatment was determined by Dr. Key(who was great too) My tech, (for the lack of her correct title) was caring, empathetic and wonderful at explaining answers to all my questions! Thank you both very much! This is the 2nd time I’ve had use an emergency vet, and each time my little guys received great care and attention at Veg.

The staff here was incredibly kind, professional, and compassionate during a stressful emergency with my cat. They treated us with respect and helped me understand payment options when I was worried about affording the care. I’m truly grateful for everyone who helped us and for the kindness they showed during a difficult moment.

So I called to check if they could take my ferret in for an emergency procedure. Their website says they do attend to "exotics" including ferrets. Anyway, the guy I talked to hem-hawed around about whether or not a particular procedure on my ferret could be done. I didn't get a straight answer. Instead, he asked if I could take my ferret to a different location miles away. (I am less than a mile away from the facility I called...Camelback location in Phoenix, AZ). But that's not what made my jaw drop in disbelief. What surprised me was the reason they couldn't take my ferret in. Supposedly one of the employees has a "life-threatening allergy" to ferrets!  What?!....You're a ER vet hospital advertising exotics care...including ferrets, and you hire someone who can't be around animals?  Give me a frickin' break. Glad I "ferreted" out this bogus ER vet business.
The most compassionate, efficient, and competent place I've ever taken my dog to. I would recommend this to anyone needed urgent or emergent care for their pet.

I took a dying kitten there, it wasn't eating. It wasn't drinking. I don't have a medical degree and I could tell it was dying. They took it in the back, brought it out and said that it ate and sent him home with me. I looked at them before I left and I said is this cat dying and they told me no. When I woke up in the morning he was dying for sure and I took him back and they told me there was nothing they could do but humanely let it die unless I wanted to pay for life-saving treatment. Do not take dying strays here. They don't care about them.

Amazing experience with VEG when we brought in our 5 year old Samoyed with a mouth wound. I love that you get to stay with your pet the entire time and how communicative and friendly the staff was! This definitely made a scary experience so much more comforting and hopefully we don’t have to return any time soon, but if that day comes we will be coming back.

I want to say a big thank you to all and every staff member we encountered while visiting VEG ER. Each and everyone we met were so helpful, kind, caring and made my family feel comfortable and confident that our best friend Ghost received the best quality of care he possibly could! We are so happy to have him home resting in his bed. Thank you so much!

I brought my cat in this morning, and I was extremely scared and on the verge of tears because I thought he had a urinary blockage. Luckily, we caught his issues before it got to that stage, but I just wanted to profoundly thank everyone who helped me this morning. Everyone was so kind and considerate to both me and my cat, and that made such a world of difference in such a high-stress situation.

My dog ate a bunch of chicken wing bones and the internet said to take him to the vet immediately.

I called this place and they put a doctor on the phone who gave me 10 minutes of her time and helped me triage it on the spot at no charge.

Very thankful for such a wonderful staff. I wish more vets were like this group.

I’m so grateful for Cat and Logan. They were absolutely amazing and took such great care of my baby during one of the most stressful moments I’ve ever experienced. They were kind, compassionate, patient, and made me feel like King was in the best hands possible. They took the time to answer my questions, kept me informed, and truly cared about both my dog and me. I can’t thank them enough for everything they did. If you’re ever in the unfortunate position of needing an emergency vet, I hope you have people like Cat and Logan taking care of you. Thank you both for making such a scary situation a little easier.
They really care about our animals and they allow you to be with your pet most of the time

Hi Brittany,

5 stars!!! They are amazing and took great care of my dog Ellie. They were very helpful and ran multiple tests and discovered there were foreign objects in my dog. Originally she was going to have to get put under for a scope to go inside and remove the objects. They ended up getting another set of scans and were able to avoid having to put her under as they could see the objects made it to the cologne. I had already signed off on the scope at this point, but I am so appreciative they checked again and were able to avoid putting her under since the objects would come out naturally. They kept her on fluids and she’s doing much better today. I cannot thank Dr Rivera (may be spelt wrong) and team enough. They are so caring and talk through everything with you and made a scary experience a lot better. Thank you again!

Third time here and every visit has been an amazing experience. Compassionate and knowledgeable this entire team goes beyond to give the best care possible. Thanks can’t say enough good things about this clinic. I hope you never need it but if you do, go here knowing you are in caring hands.

The staff here are literal angels. Luckily my dog had a minor emergency today so had a lot of time to wait in triage and observe while they treated other more severe pets. The compassion and professionalism of the staff brought tears to my eyes. They were great at communicating and providing updates to me and provided lots of at home care advice after. I hope I don’t have to return to an emergency vet anytime soon, but would absolutely choose this location again if needed.

The team at VEG showed me an extraordinary level of compassion during one of the hardest moments of my life. While saying goodbye to my beloved dog, Cecilia, every person I encountered treated us with kindness, respect, and genuine care.

Special thanks to Dr. Steven Butt, Zoe, and Fabian for their empathy, professionalism, and support. They made an incredibly painful experience a little easier to bear, and I will always be grateful for the care they showed us.

Highly recommend VEG to anyone seeking compassionate emergency veterinary care.
I want to say thank you to everyone for helping my dog today. I was so scared when I got there and you guys help me figure everything out.   I appreciate you all so much.

Our 12 yr old ate something that we assume really scratched her throat, she was coughing choking noises, super anxious and I was scared she’d eaten something poisonous. Staff was amazing, took us right back for triage and determined she wasn’t too serious, they attended to much sicker patients. While taking care of one poor fellow I looked at pup and noticed she was really calming down. While she was clearly getting better, vet tech and I determined whatever was with her wasn’t a real emergency and we went home. I’m so glad they were caring, available and helpful.

Veg was happy to help me when my dog unexpectedly got into a scary amount of dark chocolate. They saw us right away and were very friendly and efficient in helping my dude feel better. So extremely grateful for them!!
Very professional diagnosed problem set treatment plan.
The entire team is amazing.
They quickly and professionally took care of my dog.

I want to thank Dr. Madi Barton and nurse Zoe and all the nurses for everything they did for  My Cat 🐈 Kitty Ponce .
As soon as I arrived, everyone was so helpful and really show that they cared. It was my first time ever taking my cat to an emergency vet and let me tell you all of them are just awesome over there. Thank you again everyone for taking good care of us and kitty send his love he’s doing great. 🙏🏼🐈❤️

This VET emergency location is truly the best. They are so compassionate, timely, collaborative and supportive during a visit. While emergency vet situations are difficult to navigate, they take their time to ensure you understand what is happening with your pet and what the options are so that you can make a true informed decision about your pets care. Sedation for a Frenchie is very difficult and they took so much time and care to make sure he could breathe and handle procedures without issue.

I wish these providers and techs were primary care as I would not hesitate to take my sweet puppies to them for their standard care. With three “Bo’s” being cared for at once, there was no time they were confused. Our Bo received so much love and support while we navigated his swollen gland. He is now home and snuggling with his sister.

Thank you for all that you do. You’re truly amazing individuals!

We are so grateful to VEG for being available to see our sonoran desert tortoise right away! We drove all the way from Prescott Valley, after calling every vet in our area (vets were either closed or did not see reptiles). VEG gave us an immediate assessment upon seeing Hartford's injury and gave him pain meds as they said he was most likely in a lot of pain. While difficult to hear, they recommended to think about his quality of life, as his lung appeared to be damaged, and he might not live through the night to see a reptile specialist for shell surgery. They kept him warm while we debated what to do. After doing a little research on our own, we decided it was best to euthanize him. They escorted us to a peaceful, dimly lit room and gave us as much time as we needed to say goodbye to him. They then administered the sedation shot, we waited about 5 minutes, and they came back to take him to a separate area to give him the euthanasia shot. They brought him back when they were done, and we opted to take his body home with us so we could bury him. Thank you VEG for being there for us and for helping Hartford to pass as peacefully and painlessly as possible. 💖

My husband and his good buddy and fishing pal Nina were at the park the other day and a scary incident happened. Nina is a 2 year old Chihuahua with an incredibly sweet and loving disposition. Husband turned away for just a moment to speak with the game warden and heard his fishing pole move. He glanced around and Ms Nina had swallowed the treble hook that was surrounded by catfish powerbait. He clipped the line and called me in a frantic state. I looked up Emergency Pet Hospitals. Came upon VEG and decided to go there because it was close.
By the time husband reached the clinic, he was hysterically weeping. He felt so guilty even though it wasn't his fault. She's a dog and catfish powerbait probably smells delicious to a dog.
At the moment of arrival to the clinic, the staff displayed an amazing level attention and care. Not only for Nina, but for her Daddy too. It's so special there because they allow you to remain with your pet at all times.
They x-rayed her and the hook was located in her esophagus.
We had 2 choices...surgery or the Great Beyond.
The veterinarian was Victoria, she is an angel incarnate. We were so stressed out with the decisions that need to be made. She gave us space, loving encouragement and guided us to the conclusion to at least try and save her with surgery.
With steady hands, Victoria pushed the hook into her stomach, being careful not to tear any tissue on the way. She exposed her stomach, made an incision, and got the hook out without further incident.
Victoria carefully stitched her up and off to the recovery area.
Nina was highly medicated and high AF, so she had no clue what was going on. Britney made up a little area for me so that I could spend the night with Nina next to me.
The love never wavered at any point while we were in the clinic for over 12 hours. Not just for us, but for EVERYONE that walked through the door.
I would definitely recommend this place for anyone that needs a loving place to take their furry friends.

Thank you to the staff here for taking care of my dog, they were all so friendly and helpful. Pet emergencies are always scary but they did a great job of seeing us quickly, explaining everything and taking great care of my dog. Dr. Schwertner and the staff were amazing, thank you!
Super kind people here ! We found some strays they immediately helped us and took care of them
Great service they cared for not only my pet but my comfort in a long wait because they were very busy with many pet families and those who needed extra support they were amazing

Hi Francesca,

Thank you for your wonderful 5-star rating! 

Nichole Collen, Hospital Manager
These people are truly amazing ! Took good care of my puppy when she ate garlic! Very understanding and they work with you.

I love VEG, I called, they were absolutely kind, helpful and informative about issues my dog was facing.  Honestly in a world where increasingly you feel like just a number or a wallet, the personal and caring touch was everything I needed.  What a solid group of professionals and clearly an ethically driven company!

This was one of the best vet experiences we've had. And that's saying something, because we've been dog owners for 14 years, and one of those dogs has had emergency surgery before and a host of health issues resulting from it. We had to stop in because he needed to be induced to vomit after ingesting something harmful, and the entire team from the front desk to the techs and doctor were awesome.

Our Pup NEEDLESSLY Suffered In Front of Our Eyes Last Evening in the Emergency Room Before He Took His Gasps of Air and went to Doggie Heaven.

He was almost 17-years-old and suffered from congestive heart failure. I had taken him into the same VEG Camelback location the week prior knowing his health was rapidly declining and that euthanasia was a high and likely probability.

Fortunately, the veterinarians were able to help our boy breathe more easily and efficiently, despite the fact that he had to be treated for significant water retention in his lungs due to his condition.

I was able to bring him home to my wife, who had to work, with the understanding that he probably only had three-to-six months to live. We were fine with that including footing the very large bill.

In the end, we felt like we bought more time with our elderly pup and the hefty price was worth it. My wife and I still feel this way despite VEG’s great failure last night that now leaves us devastated.

Unfortunately, our dog’s ability to overcome the water accumulation in his lungs was not sustainable. We drove back to VEG fulling knowing that our precious pup should probably be euthanized. We waited in the room with our boy for the vet for quite a long while.

During that time, his condition got worse to the point that he appeared to have died in my wife’s arms. I raced out to the room and yelled that my dog just died. It was only then that the veterinarian and another staff member rushed into the room. My wife decided my baby boy had suffered long enough and it was time for us to say goodbye.

We are not upset with the final outcome as we had already come to terms with the decision. But the needless suffering our dog had to endure leading up to his death while we patiently waited for the vet was beyond ridiculous.

We were told that the veterinarian had another pet in a critical state she had been attending to. This was the reason that she was not able to get to our pup sooner. We can certainly understand and appreciate the difficulties of these circumstances. At the same time, the emergency room was well aware of our dog’s condition, ESPECIALLY the vet who had initially treated him the week prior.

We are NOT singling out that veterinarian or the vet who eventually euthanized our pup. There is enough blame to be spread around for the entire facility. To be placed in the room and have ABSOLUTELY NO ONE check on our dog’s condition is unacceptable and a dismal failure.

To be fair and objective, we felt this vet emergency room was top notch during our initial visit. We told the front desk our dog collapsed and the staff rushed us in with a sense of urgency and without hesitation. In fact, our impression was that this is way better service than one experiences at hospitals for humans. Unfortunately, that opinion dramatically changed for the worse last evening.

It’s really difficult to express our frustrations without lashing out in anger as I did last night when VEG failed us. But hopefully pet owners who read this post can absorb this information objectively to determine whether they should bring their pet here or somewhere else.

Took our 14.5 year old dog in Tues night into Weds morning because we knew he had a heart murmur that had worsened over the years (had likely become CHF). He had been crying in pain as he panted, would have difficulty laying down comfortably, often laying on his chest, breathing through his mouth, loss of appetite (going from 35 lbs to 27 lbs), no interest in normal activities, difficulty moving around, etc. A quality of life questionnaire on Coda Pet (incredibly thorough and highly recommended) gave him a rating of 2.8 out of 40, indicating extremely poor.

We arrived and disclosed that before coming in, we looked up what could help with pain and gave him baby aspirin according to his weight. And Dr. Furtak told us it's not recommended because it could cause kidney damage (irony in this later). So we humbly asked if not aspirin according to veterinary charts, what would be a better alternative? She had no answer to alternatives, but instead said *heart murmurs don't cause pain* and aspirin just wouldn't help.

Dr. Christina Furtak wanted a whole work up costing $1,400. Can't afford that with a third baby on the way, gas prices out the roof, and inflation, whatnot (you know, we're all feeling it). The combination of medications she was recommending wasn't affordable for us either. So we asked what we can do for comfort care. She lowered the price to do the scans, but it still wouldn't change the outcome. *IF* the meds could be afforded, it wouldn't fix the late-stage murmur and would prolong the problem, possibly adding complications (she needed blood work to ensure his kidneys were functioning enough to take the meds, which she was somehow willing to bypass if she could just do scans - a little ironic, eh?). We reiterated the desire for comfort care and asked what we could do at home. She did nothing. Absolutely nothing. She discharged and sent him home, allowing him to suffer.

Our poor guy came home, still wouldn't eat, drink, eat favorite treats, stopped moving around, had accidents on himself, and sometimes wouldn't even want to lift/turn his head for his name. It got worse so rapidly, we had to take him in some place else Friday evening for an urgent euthanasia, because we knew he wouldn't make it through the weekend to a Monday euthanasia appointment (still somewhere else) and we couldn't bear to see him suffer another day.

The vet we ended up taking him to for peaceful passing didn't need some crazy work up to realize he was suffering and didn't need scans to know how bad the heart murmur had become. It was so severe, *she could feel it when touching his chest*, stating it was definitely a grade 5 or 6 - didn't even need a stethoscope. She could see the same protruding spine, the same treat refusal, etc, so what on earth was the excuse?

Instead, the veterinarian immediately said she suspected RHDV2 (a serious viral disease) and began discussing an extensive and very expensive treatment plan including a CT scan, IV fluids, viral testing, bloodwork, and more. I repeatedly explained that this appeared to be an acute physical issue, not a virus, but I felt like my concerns were dismissed and the conversation focused mainly on costly diagnostics.
I also left feeling that the staff did not seem very knowledgeable about rabbit care. The technician taking his intake information did not know what breed of rabbit he was, he is a Holland Lop, one of the most common domestic rabbit breeds. That immediately made me uneasy about their familiarity with rabbit specific emergencies.
At the end of the visit, while I was paying, the veterinarian came back and said she would do an X-ray in case he had aspirated. This was mentioned after no stabilization or direct treatment had been done, and by that point my rabbit was no longer in active respiratory distress. The overall approach just did not match what I was seeing with my animal.
Because I didn’t feel his immediate needs were being addressed, I chose to leave. Despite no treatment being provided, I was still charged $190.
The next day, I took him to his regular veterinarian because he had stopped eating and wasn’t producing stool. He was diagnosed with GI stasis and given a clear, reasonable treatment plan. They specifically said they did NOT suspect any viral illness.
My experience at VEG felt rushed, dismissive, and heavily focused on expensive testing rather than addressing the obvious issue in front of them. I left feeling unheard and worried, and I do not feel the exam fee was justified given that no care was actually provided.
Rabbit owners, I would strongly recommend seeking a rabbit experienced vet if possible.

As a pet owner, I trusted that the emergency clinic would act in the best interest of my dog. Instead, I felt pressured into making a devastating decision that was presented as inevitable — when it clearly was not.

That this incident is investigated.

That the clinic’s policies and procedures for recommending euthanasia are reviewed.

That further oversight is placed on staff who make such irreversible and critical decisions.
